title: PROGRAMME_5 TRADE IN THE COUNTY
subject: social-studies
text:
1 ” to allow audio playback TRADE IN THE COUNTY [Music] Hello Learner, Welcome to Social Studies for grade four. Today, we shall talk about trade in the county. Your radio teacher is Esther Simaloi. Welcome to the program. [Music]

2 ” to allow audio playback Hello Grade 4 learner. Welcome to our social studies lesson. Today, we are going to learn about the methods of trade used in the county and the benefits of trade in the county. First, let us remind ourselves what we learnt in the previous lesson. What did we say economic activities are? #Bell# We said economic activities are the things that people do to make money. Learner name some economic activities people do in your county? Name some economic activities people do in your county. #Bell# Well done. I hope your answers include Trading Fishing. Fishing Tourism, Mining, Farming and Forestry Among the economic activities you have just mentioned is trading. Can you remember what trading is? Can you remember what trading is? #Bell# Good Trading involves people buying and selling of goods and services. In today's lesson, we shall discuss about trade in the county. Trade is the buying and selling of goods and services. People sell what they have in plenty and buy what they do not have. There are two types of trade, namely; Barter trade Currency trade Let us talk about barter trade, barter trade is the exchange of goods for goods. In the past, people in your county exchanged goods for goods, Which goods do you think they exchanged? Which goods do you think they exchanged? #Bell# People used to exchange goods which they produced with what they did not produce. These enabled them to get what they did not have. People traveled far to look for someone to exchange what they had with what they did not have. Barter trade was mainly used in the past. Learner, do people in your county still practice barter trade today? Do people in your county still practice barter trade today? #Bell#

3 ” to allow audio playback Today things have changed and people in your county use money to buy the things they need. This type of trade is currency trade. Repeat after me, currency trade. #Bell# Currency trade is the use of money to pay for goods and services. People use money to buy what they need. Money is the medium of exchange. How do people in your county pay for things they buy? How do people in your county pay for things they buy? #Bell# Well done. I hope your answers include; Mobile phones, Cards, Cheques, Where does trade take place in your county? Where does trade take place in your county? #Bell# Trade takes place in a trading center, a shopping center or a commercial center. A trading center is a place with many shops and kiosks where people buy and sell their goods and services, which is the nearest shopping center in your area. Which is the nearest shopping center in your area. #Bell# Does it have many shops? Does it have many shops? #Bell# Which goods are sold in your shopping center? Which goods are sold in your shopping center? #Bell# Trade is very important. Trade in your county has the following benefits. It provides job opportunities to people in the county. It provides job opportunities to people in the county. It is a source of income to many traders. It is a source of income to many traders. It leads to development of roads which are used for transport. It leads to development of roads which are used for transport. It also leads to development of communication, network It helps us to make good use of our resources. It helps us to make good use of our resources. It promotes cooperation and understanding among the people who are trading together. This in turn, brings respect between people in your county. How else is trade important? How else is trade important? #Bell# Just as trade is important in our county, it is always good to remember that you should do lawful activities in your county. Illegal trade activities are harmful to our people. Share with your friends things that you can buy from your nearest market. That marks the end of our lesson today. Until next time. Goodbye.
